div.span: - Compose brings up Redis and the origin, then runs the student app in the chosen language on the same network.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 129px; margin-left: 1093px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.span: - The app sends GET product:N to Redis on port 6379. A cache hit answers in under 5 ms and the origin is never called.

div.b: On a miss, call the origin

div.span: - The app calls GET /products/N on the Python API, which sleeps 500 ms on every request to stand in for a slow database.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 38px; height: 1px; padding-top: 285px; margin-left: 1093px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #FFFFFF;

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;

div.span: - The app writes the response back with SET product:N, so the next request for that key is a hit.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 578px; height: 1px; padding-top: 502px; margin-left: 1110px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.span: - Only the app container is edited: the four caching patterns and the eviction tasks are all written there.
- Redis and the origin stay as shipped, so every measured difference comes from the cache logic, not from the environment.
